summary: Pre-market, Monday 2026-09-21. The risk score eased 0.54 to 44.55, holding at caution inside a goldilocks regime, and the move is a discount-rate story rather than a growth one: the Treasury curve repriced 7 basis points lower in parallel, across the 10-year at 4.94, the 2-year at 4.67 and the 10-year real rate at 2.61, while breakevens barely moved with the 5Y5Y forward at 2.35 and the 10-year at 2.33. The administered rate finally caught up in the data, the effective federal funds rate printing 3.88 against 3.63 previously, yet the FedWatch-implied policy rate at 4.155 still prices a hike. The energy impulse reversed decisively: WTI fell 3.26% to 92.950 dollars a barrel, a two-week low, unwinding part of the supply-shock premium that dominated the past three weeks. The last completed US session was a hardware rebound, semiconductor equipment at 4.0704, memory at 2.7866 and semis at 2.7312 against AI software at -2.0287, but only 11 of 22 sectors and themes closed higher. The tracked A-share panel closed 9 of 11 names higher, led by 300475.sz at 5.0941 and 688008.sh at 3.7377, while crypto re-rated with Bitcoin at 84325, up 4.93265. Model confidence 0.9158. Watch the FOMC on 2026-09-28, PCE and GDP on 2026-09-30, and the state visit of China's president to the United States from 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-25.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The discount rate is still the binding constraint even after this week's repricing: the 10-year real rate at 2.61 sits at the 99.84th percentile and the 10-year yield at 4.94 at the 99.44th, keeping the macro block the heaviest at 64.36.

The administered and the market rate diverged: the effective federal funds rate now prints 3.88 after 3.63, the secured overnight financing rate rose to 3.85, yet the 2-year yield eased from 4.74 to 4.67 and the FedWatch-implied policy rate at 4.155 still discounts a hike.

The energy supply-shock premium is being unwound: WTI fell 3.26% to 92.950 dollars a barrel, the lowest in two weeks, Brent fell 2.54% to 96.769, and Washington is pressing Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries, the same impulse behind the past three weeks of breakeven and diesel headlines.

Internal structure has not repaired: only 0.0065 of the universe printed a new 52-week high against 0.0129 printing new lows, 0.5871 sit above the 200-day average, and semiconductor relative strength at -18.6382 and small-cap relative strength at -5.8892 remain deeply negative.

Leadership inside the AI complex split cleanly, hardware bid and software offered: semiconductor equipment at 4.0704, memory at 2.7866, semis at 2.7312 and data centers at 2.289 against AI software at -2.0287, cybersecurity at -1.7608 and cloud computing at -1.4417, leaving only 11 of 22 sectors and themes higher.

supporting_signals.claim: Volatility is the calmest block in the model: the VIX at 15.44 sits at only the 26.75th percentile, realized volatility is 9.175 and the volatility dimension reads 18.93.
Credit refuses to price stress: high-yield spreads hold at 2.70, the 11.31st percentile, and investment-grade spreads at 0.78, the 17.94th.
Crypto shows risk appetite intact: Bitcoin at 84325, up 4.93265, Ethereum at 2714.38, up 5.40241, and SOL at 115.67, up 6.9217.
Trend structure remains constructive: price sits 6.3395 percent above the 200-day moving average, only -2.0813 percent below the 52-week high, with 3-month momentum at 2.002.
The bond rally is a real-rate move, not an inflation-expectations one: the 10-year breakeven held at 2.33 and the 5Y5Y forward at 2.35 even as nominal and real yields fell.

contradicting_signals.claim: Cross-asset confirmation fell to 0.5, so only half of the tracked signals agree on direction, which does not square with a bond market rallying while crypto gains more than 4 percent.
The composite fell 0.54 even as yields fell 7 basis points, because the macro, equity-structure and trend blocks all carry a falling trend while liquidity, volatility and cross-asset sit flat.
A-shares did not mirror the US software weakness: 9 of 11 tracked names closed higher, led by 300475.sz at 5.0941 and 688008.sh at 3.7377, a momentum signature rather than a fundamental one.

Fed communication runs against the bond market: Goolsbee said restoring price stability will not be smooth sailing and that the only route back to balance is to suppress demand, with the FedWatch-implied policy rate at 4.155 still pricing a hike.
The news layer's highest-importance item is a Fed speech at 59.97, ahead of the crude oil report at 49.97, so the press flow offers little independent explanation for the sector split.

what_changed_today: The risk score eased 0.54 to 44.55, holding at caution with a goldilocks regime and a weekly change of -0.66.
The whole Treasury curve fell 7 basis points: the 10-year from 5.01 to 4.94, the 2-year from 4.74 to 4.67 and the 10-year real rate from 2.68 to 2.61.
The effective federal funds rate moved to 3.88 from 3.63, the first data confirmation of the delivered hike, while the secured overnight financing rate rose to 3.85.
WTI crude fell 3.26% to 92.950 dollars a barrel, a two-week low, the first decisive break in the supply-shock narrative of the past three weeks.
Leadership rotated back into AI hardware: semiconductor equipment at 4.0704 and memory at 2.7866 against AI software at -2.0287, with 11 of 22 sectors and themes closing higher.
Bitcoin rose 4.93265 to 84325, and the overnight reverse repo balance rose to 0.576 from 0.276, a small refill of a facility that had been nearly drained.
watch_next: The FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28 is the next policy test, with the FedWatch-implied policy rate at 4.155 already pricing a hike.
Personal income and outlays, including the PCE price index, together with GDP on 2026-09-30 test whether disinflation can coexist with growth resilience.
The employment report on 2026-10-02 will decide whether the market must revise hike-path pricing higher once more.
The state visit of China's president to the United States from 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-25 is the key political hurdle for equities inside the window.
Costco earnings on 2026-09-24, and the breadth reading still at 0.0065 of names making new 52-week highs, are the two gauges to watch for a durable repair.

bull_case.title: Bull case: the real-rate retreat extends and hardware leadership broadens
points: If the 2026-09-30 PCE and GDP prints confirm disinflation, the real rate can retreat further from 2.61 and valuations regain room.

The hardware complex re-established leadership, semiconductor equipment at 4.0704, memory at 2.7866 and semis at 2.7312, while breadth above the 200-day average already improved to 0.5871 from 0.5548.
The VIX at 15.44, the 26.75th percentile, alongside Bitcoin up 4.93265, shows risk appetite still has room to run.

base_case.title: Base case: rates stay near their extremes and the score churns near 45
points: A macro block at 64.36 and a real rate at 2.61, the 99.84th percentile, cap the upside, so the score is more likely to churn around 44.55.
With the FedWatch-implied policy rate at 4.155 pricing a hike, sector rotation rather than overall valuation will drive returns, exactly as the 11 of 22 split showed.
The energy unwind strips out an inflation hedge but also removes a supply-shock tail risk, leaving WTI at 92.950 as a broadly neutral input.

bear_case.title: Bear case: the front end reprices higher and breadth fails to repair
points: A 7-basis-point rally in yields is relief, not repair: the real rate at 2.61 is still the 99.84th percentile and the 10-year at 4.94 the 99.44th, so any hawkish FOMC surprise re-imposes the constraint immediately.
Breadth has not repaired: only 0.0065 of names made a new 52-week high against 0.0129 making new lows, with semiconductor relative strength at -18.6382 and small-cap relative strength at -5.8892.
Cross-asset confirmation at only 0.5 leaves bonds and equities without a common direction, and an 11 of 22 split means half the market is already falling.
